old_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene of a large, dark storm cloud system moving across a vast, arid landscape. The sky is filled with thick, ominous clouds that range from deep gray to lighter shades, indicating varying moisture levels and intensity. As the video progresses, the clouds appear to be advancing towards the horizon, suggesting an impending storm. The landscape below is flat and barren, dotted with sparse vegetation typical of a desert or semi-arid region. In the distance, faint outlines of hills or mountains can be seen, adding depth to the scene. The overall atmosphere is tense and foreboding, with the dark clouds dominating the sky and casting shadows over the landscape. There are no visible animals or characters in the video; the focus remains solely on the natural elements. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to observe the gradual movement of the clouds and the subtle changes in lighting and shadow as the storm approaches.

caption: The video captures an arid desert plain beneath a low, heavy storm cloud deck, with a flat horizon, a small mesa at left, and scattered shrubs fixed throughout. A bright rain shaft hangs on the right side of the frame, and a dark finger of cloud protrudes downward from the central cloud base. The clouds continuously churn and deform, their undersides undulating and reorganizing from frame to frame. The bright gap in the upper sky shifts shape and brightness, while small blue patches appear and fade within it. The central lowering, already present at the start, elongates and thickens through the early and middle frames, then persists as a hanging mass creeping slowly rightward. The rain shaft remains visible the whole time, its column edges widening and contracting as the cloud system moves across the sky. No visible motion touches the desert floor, so the movement appears confined to the churning clouds and precipitation. The lowering remains suspended beneath the rolling deck while the rain shaft continues falling at right.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

draft_caption: The video captures a static view of an arid desert plain beneath a low, heavy storm cloud deck, with a flat horizon, a small mesa at left, and scattered shrubs fixed throughout. A bright rain shaft hangs on the right side of the frame, and a dark finger of cloud protrudes downward from the central cloud base. The clouds continuously churn and deform, their undersides undulating and reorganizing from frame to frame. The bright gap in the upper sky shifts shape and drifts toward the center and top, while small blue patches appear and fade within it. The central lowering, already present at the start, elongates and thickens through the early and middle frames, then persists as a hanging mass creeping slowly rightward. The rain shaft remains visible the whole time, its column edges widening and contracting as the cloud system tracks across the sky. No motion touches the desert floor, confirming that the movement belongs entirely to the churning clouds and precipitation. The lowering remains suspended beneath the rolling deck while the rain shaft continues falling at right.
